text.p: U.S. investment bank Merrill Lynch said on Monday it had raised its intermediate share rating for German chemical group Hoechst from "neutral" to "accumulate".
"That means that we think Hoechst is undervalued but not dramatically so," Merrill's London-based chemical analyst Shaw Bridges said in response to enquiries.
Merrill's long-term rating for the group remains "buy" and the bank sees a near-term level for its shares of 80 marks and a two-year rating of 100 marks.
He said the raising of the intermediate rating was a response to the perception that a greater focus by Hoechst in its life sciences business would enhance cash-flow and earnings quality.
Shares in Hoechst were traded 91 pfennigs higher at 67.0 marks by 0742 GMT in electronic IBIS trade.
